summary: Iteration 14 verified the two frontend workarounds for the backend gaps found in iteration 13. Both FIX-4 (on-time alert derived from `wait`) and FIX-6 (address+map-link pack/unpack) now work end-to-end. All 4 branches of FIX-4 exercised via response interception (matching-id+wait=0, matching-id+wait=3 shows banner, matching-id+wait=8 no banner, mismatched-id no banner). FIX-6 confirmed live: provider saved map link → reload → both fields populated correctly; backend `address` column now stores the packed string; customer sees plain address + Get Directions button pointing to the map URL (target=_blank). All regressions pass.

minor.issue: Provider model still has no location_link column — frontend workaround (packAddress) makes this non-blocking, but a first-class column would eliminate the '\n\n📍 ' marker inside the address string.

Still (a) has no explicit `position` field and (b) ignores provider_id/date query params (returns customer's next active booking globally). Frontend workaround now derives position from `wait` and gates on booking-id match, so functional issues are resolved. Backend correction would still be nicer.

critical_code_review_comments: packAddress marker '\n\n📍 ' is stored inside the address column verbatim. If any admin/exports view the raw provider records they'll see the emoji + URL appended. Fine for now, but worth documenting in the Provider schema comment for the next dev.

unpackAddress fallback (regex trailing http URL + isMapUrl host check) is a good defensive touch — legacy addresses that had a bare URL appended will still be split cleanly without needing a data migration.

BookingDetail.jsx L54 `if (["pending","confirmed","in_progress"].includes(b.status))` — for `pending` bookings that haven't been assigned a token yet, calling /queue/my-position with a mismatched-id fallback is a wasted request. Consider gating the call on `booking.token_number != null` to reduce noise.

Route interception showed the backend `/queue/my-position` ignores provider_id/date — this remains a latent risk if a customer with multiple active bookings looks at the non-first one: the derived position would be wrong. The current mismatch-id guard correctly hides the position UI in that case, which is safer than showing wrong data. Good defensive coding.
action_items: No action required for iteration 14 goals — both target workarounds function correctly end-to-end.
Optional cleanup: request backend team to add a first-class `location_link` column so we can drop the packAddress workaround.
Optional cleanup: request backend team to add a `position` integer + honor provider_id/date on /queue/my-position; then simplify BookingDetail.jsx to read qp.position directly.
Optional testability: seed a receptionist account linked to QuickWheels (Automobile) so the auto walk-in branch and receptionist reorder arrows can be validated live in future iterations.
